newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to repay remaining U.S. Treasury loan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to repay remaining U.S. Treasury loan.

text.p: Mexico will announce plans in a few minutes to repay the remainder of a $12.5 billion emergency loan it received in February 1995 from the United States, a Finance Ministry official said Wednesday.
Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz was due to announce the repayment program at a ceremony in the presidential palace Wednesday morning, said the official, who asked not to be identified.
Finance ministry officials said some $3.5 billion remained to be paid by Mexico to the U.S. Treasury.

The loan was extended by Washington in February 1995 to shore up the Mexican economy in the wake of a catastrophic devaluation of the peso in December 1994 which plunged the country into a deep recession and almost caused it to default.
Mexico first repaid $2 billion of the loan and last July it repaid another $7 billion, leaving $3.5 billion outstanding.
